what: Model-judge results for blind panels 1 and 2, recorded separately from human ratings
kind: MODEL JUDGES, not human raters. No human rating exists yet for either panel; when one does, it is reported beside this and does not replace it.
authority: The author's instruction, verbatim, 2026-10-10: "I want you to be the blind judge". This amends both protocols (evidence/shaders-comparison-protocol.json, evidence/shaders-lab2-panel-protocol.json), which had said model judges are not used. The amendment was written before any rating existed.
design: Three fresh model agents per panel with no conversation context (two on the session model, one on a different tier). Each saw only anonymised images and a trials file; none saw the key, the code or any report. GIF clips were also shown as 12-frame strips. Vote files were hashed before the keys were opened. Metric and decision rule unchanged (Wilson 95%; preferred only when the lower bound is above 0.5).
does_not_prove: The intervals are too narrow: repeats are near copies and the three judges are one model family, so the effective number of independent judgements is near the number of distinct pairs.
The judges are the same model family that built the shaders; shared biases can favour the same look. A model preference is not a human preference.
Panel 2 compares each technique with itself switched off, not with any product.
Motion was judged from 12-frame strips, so the sag and hysteresis results are weak.
No claim of superiority over any product follows (the protocols' claim rule).

follow_up_dither_loss.finding: Diagnosed 2026-10-10 on the panel's own scene card (EGA, bayer4). The vendored ordered dither (retro-dither.js orderedPick) picks the nearest palette colour and a far-side colour and sets the mixing fraction by projection in OKLab. A dither is averaged by the eye in linear light, so an OKLab fraction over-weights the brighter colour in the darks. Region means on the grey ramp (source -> ours): 13 -> 27 (blue cast), 20 -> 57, 32 -> 64, 48 -> 74. The competitor's per-channel Bayer keeps those near black. A linear-light fraction on the same pair cut the mean region error from 17.8 to 10.0 codes (patches and ramp, 16 regions). Saturated colours on EGA (a yellow patch went grey-green) also suffer from the two-colour pair choice, which a per-channel threshold on an RGB-cube palette like EGA avoids.
follow_up_dither_loss.status: Not changed. The ordered modes are bound to retro-dither.js bit for bit (M1 criterion 10), so a fix is a new mixing option with its own bounds and parity, and the choice of default is the author's. Recommended: a linear-light fraction option, then decide the default.
